item.title: UK vows anti-settler measures as Israel warns of retaliation
item.description:
Britain's foreign secretary vowed a tough response to "appalling" violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank on Tuesday, drawing threats from Israel that it would retaliate if the UK imposed sanctions.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing allies have been ramping up support for settlements in the run-up to close-fought elections, despite increasing attacks by extremist settlers who seek to drive out Palestinians.

item.title: US strikes Iran in latest tit-for-tat attacks
item.description:
US forces struck Iran's Revolutionary Guards on Tuesday in response to attempted attacks on commercial shipping and American troops, the US military said, with President Donald Trump vowing a tough response to any counter-attacks.

The strikes were the latest in a series of attacks by both US and Iranian forces in recent days that threaten to reignite the simmering conflict.

Iranian state television reported that several explosions were heard in the country's south along the strategic Strait of Hormuz waterway.

item.title: IAEA reports progress in Syria investigation, none in Iran
item.description:
By Francois Murphy

VIENNA, Sept 1 (Reuters) - The U.N. nuclear watchdog has resolved its outstanding questions in an investigation into secret nuclear activities in Syria under the Assad family's rule but made no progress in Iran, it said on Tuesday in confidential reports seen by Reuters.

item.title: More than 10 EU countries willing to contribute to Lebanon mission
item.description:
BRUSSELS, Sept 1 (Reuters) - More than 10 European Union members are willing to contribute resources and people to a planned ​mission to advise and train Lebanon's armed forces, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Tuesday.

The proposed mission stems from the EU studying ways to strengthen Lebanese forces to help free up the Lebanese ​army to focus on disarming the armed group Hezbollah.

item.title: China's Xi lands in Egypt as Iran war reshapes Middle East alliances
item.description:
CAIRO, Sept 1 (Reuters) - Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Egypt on Tuesday, his first visit to the Arab world's most populous nation in a decade, as countries across the Middle East reassess security and economic ties amid the fallout of the Iran war.

The conflict has disrupted global energy markets and raised questions about whether regional countries can count on the United States as a long-term security partner.

item.title: Trump says latest strikes on Iran are 'justified,' warns Tehran against retaliation
item.description:
Sept 1 (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the latest U.S. attack on Iran was "justified," and threatened bigger strikes if Tehran retaliated.

Trump, in a Truth Social post, said the U.S. military was striking Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday in retaliation for Iran's "failed attempt at adding sea mines" to the Strait and for shooting eight missiles at a U.S. military base in Jordan.

(Reporting by Bhargav Acharya, Susan Heavey and Ismail Shakil;Editing by David Ljunggren)

item.title: US airstrikes target Iran's Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island
item.description: American military forces launched their first strikes on the Iranian mainland in more than a month just days after the top US commander for the region said Iranian mines have been cleared from Hormuz shipping lanes.

item.title: Israeli strikes kill four in operation to seize Hamas figure in Gaza: officials
item.description:
Heavy Israeli bombardment killed four people in Gaza City on Tuesday, Palestinian health officials said, in what both sides described as an Israeli-backed ground operation to seize a senior Hamas figure.

Eyewitnesses reported around a dozen strikes on Tuesday morning in western Gaza City, where the territory's civil defence agency said four people were killed: three children and a woman.

Gaza City's Al-Shifa Hospital confirmed the toll given by the civil defence, which operates as a rescue force under Hamas.

item.title: Fresh fighting in Syria's Suwayda leaves one dead: What to know
item.description: Renewed clashes in Suwayda highlight the fragile security situation in the Druze-majority province.

item.title: UK to unveil 'comprehensive' response to Israeli West Bank settlement plans in coming weeks
item.description:
LONDON, Sept 1 (Reuters) - Britain will set out a "comprehensive" package of measures on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank in the coming weeks, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said on Tuesday.

Miliband told lawmakers that Israel's E1 settlement project would cut across land which the Palestinians seek for a state and "risks making a Palestinian state unviable".

"This government will not acquiesce in the destruction of the two-state solution," he said. "We will act and I will set out a comprehensive set of measures in the coming weeks."

item.title: Blockade succeeds where sanctions failed as Iran oil exports stall
item.description:
By Ahmad Ghaddar, Enes Tunagur and Robert Harvey

LONDON, Sept 1 (Reuters) - For the first time on record, Iran has gone about seven weeks without shipping meaningful crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz, as a U.S. naval blockade succeeds where years of sanctions failed by cutting off one of Tehran's main sources of foreign-currency earnings.

item.title: Himalayas face severe glacial flood risks in years ahead, UN official warns
item.description:
By Rick Noack

ISLAMABAD, Sept 1 (Reuters) - The Himalayan region faces severe risks from future glacial floods, a senior U.N. official has warned, as the death toll from last week's flood in Nepal, triggered by a glacier's collapse, surpassed 1,000.

Not only is the hydroelectric power that many depend on threatened, but entire riverbanks where millions live might become effectively uninhabitable.
